# Thrum Pro

> Plugins and skills that connect AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Muse, Antigravity, OpenCode)
> to Thrum, git-backed messaging and coordination for AI agents. This repository holds the plugins only; the `thrum`
> binary is distributed separately.

- Install and update steps for each runtime: https://github.com/leonletto/thrum-pro/blob/main/INSTALL.md
- Overview and getting the binary: https://github.com/leonletto/thrum-pro/blob/main/README.md
- Full command reference: `thrum --help` and `thrum <command> --help`

## Reaching an agent on a daemon you are not paired with

A message routes through a directly paired peer, never by pairing with the target daemon. The sending daemon resolves
a recipient from its local agents and from the agents registered on its directly paired peers only.

For an agent that lives on a daemon you are not paired with, run once on the SENDING daemon, per remote agent, naming
the directly paired peer that knows the agent:

    thrum peer configure <relay-peer-name> add-agent <agent-name>

Then `thrum send --to @<agent-name>` routes through that peer. Do this on each side that needs to send.

- Check pairing with `thrum peer list` (directly paired peers only).
- Check delivery with `thrum message get <id>`, which shows `(delivered)` per recipient. A send that returned without
  error is not proof of delivery.
- Not the fix: pairing the two daemons with each other.
- Not needed for delivery: `thrum peer relayed add` and `thrum peer relayed grant`, which govern what a daemon accepts
  from a relayed origin. `thrum peer relayed add --via` takes daemon IDs, not peer names; `thrum peer relayed grant`
  does not validate the capability key (the messaging key is `can_send_messages`).
- After `add-agent`, the supervisor may report "Unresolved agent records" for the proxy rows: reconcile asks the relay,
  which refuses with "owned by daemon X ... no second hop". A build with the reconcile owner pointer follows the named
  owner once and the warning clears; older builds keep the warning. Do NOT delete those rows as the supervisor
  suggests: deleting them removes the routing.

`thrum tmux send <agent> [<text>] [--keys K1,K2,...]` uses the same peer routing, for local and remote sessions alike.

Skill: `routing-messages-across-daemons`.

## Account usage (quota-axi)

Off by default. Setting `daemon.account_usage_quota_axi` to `true` in `.thrum/config.json` makes the daemon run the
pinned `quota-axi` (0.1.68, found on the daemon's own PATH, never installed by the daemon) every 15 minutes and show
used / remaining / reset time per account in `thrum team` (Accounts section).

`daemon.account_usage_runtimes` picks which runtimes are read: by default claude, codex, cursor and copilot; muse,
antigravity and opencode only when listed. Both keys are read at daemon start (`thrum daemon restart`). A daemon
without a reading shows "Usage not enabled on daemon".

Setup steps, per-runtime credentials and failure states: the `setting-up-account-usage` skill.
